summary.intent: Investigate and fix someguy v0.11.1 IPNS routing failures that caused indefinite hangs on staging, then implement a delegated-ipfs.dev fallback with Prometheus metrics for visibility.
summary.outcome: Fixed someguy configuration (DHT mode, libp2p port, resource limits), validated with E2E and load tests, implemented API-level fallback with metrics counters, and merged PR #325 after resolving all review comments.

repo: Previous someguy deployment failed due to: missing libp2p port 4004 exposure, 'standard' DHT mode instead of 'accelerated', too-tight resources (0.5 CPU/768MB RAM/512MB libp2p), and low connection limits (50/300 vs defaults 100/3000)

IPNS resolve in ipns.service.ts always queries DB after network and prefers the higher sequence number — since publish to someguy is fire-and-forget while DB write is synchronous, DB always wins, meaning 100% of resolves are served from DB even with someguy running
ThrottlerBypassGuard uses an X-Throttle-Bypass header with a secret, not NODE_ENV=test — setting NODE_ENV=test alone does not relax rate limits in E2E tests
Vitest does not auto-load .env files into process.env — env vars must be passed directly on the CLI (e.g. THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET=... pnpm test)

Mock IPNS routing service is intentionally kept for CI workflows (localhost:3001) for deterministic, offline tests — someguy is not suitable for CI due to DHT warm-up time and outbound peer bootstrapping
The .learnings/ directory in the repo root is used to capture dev insights with dated markdown files

code.finding: Comment explicitly states publish to delegated routing is fire-and-forget, making DB always ahead of DHT for sequence numbers
resolveRecord() tries network first (line 320) but always queries DB regardless (line 339), then prefers whichever has higher sequence number (lines 343-358) — DB always wins since publish is async

New fallback logic: DELEGATED_ROUTING_FALLBACK_URL env var triggers secondary attempt only after primary exhausts all retries; metrics tagged with {backend: 'primary'|'fallback', outcome: 'success'|'error'|'not_found'}

workflow: Vitest env vars must be passed on the command line, not in .env files — SOME_VAR=value pnpm exec vitest is the reliable pattern
Docker healthchecks with CMD-SHELL run inside the container, not on the host — host having wget does not mean the container image has it; curl is safer as it ships with more minimal images

CodeRabbit automated review suggestions should be empirically verified — the wget/curl flag was correct in principle but the image actually ships wget; the curl change was harmless but the flag was based on an unverified assumption
Someguy DHT routing table is cold on fresh start — load test p50 latency gap vs delegated-ipfs.dev will shrink after hours of operation as routing table fills
Prometheus counter label design: use {operation, backend, outcome} on request counter plus a separate fallbacks_total counter for easy alerting on rate(fallbacks_total[5m]) > 0

friction: E2E tests returned 429s masking actual test results — required discovering the ThrottlerBypassGuard header mechanism and that vitest doesn't load .env files
Three separate iterations needed to get E2E tests passing: setting NODE_ENV=test (ineffective), creating sdk-e2e/.env (not loaded by vitest), finally passing env var on CLI
Remote had new commits during the session requiring stash/rebase/pop before push
Background task notifications required reading separate output files to retrieve results
CodeRabbit flagged wget→curl as a defect in both docker-compose files; empirical verification on the running container showed wget was present, making the fix technically unnecessary but harmless
open_items: DB-first IPNS resolve strategy means 100% of resolves hit the database even with someguy running — optimization deferred until DB load becomes a concern; the lever is returning network result when sequence numbers match
Mock IPNS routing service left in local docker-compose alongside someguy — intentionally kept for offline/isolated dev use cases
Load test metrics JSON files were not committed to the repo (untracked) — raw baseline data for future performance regression comparison

Someguy fallback to delegated-ipfs.dev not configured at the someguy level (SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS) — decided against it since someguy does concurrent fanout not true fallback, and API-level fallback provides better metrics visibility
Grafana alert and dashboard panels for fallback metrics were specified but not yet created — rate(cipherbox_delegated_routing_fallbacks_total[5m]) > 0 alert and primary vs fallback request rate panel
